claim: HIV-1 Gag selects and packages a dimeric, unspliced viral RNA in the context of a large excess of cytosolic human RNAs.
source: HIV-1 Gag selects and packages a dimeric, unspliced viral RNA in the context of a large excess of cytosolic human RNAs.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in HIV-1 biology, drawing from established scientific consensus.

claim: A minimal system consisting of purified RNAs, recombinant HIV-1 Gag and giant unilamellar vesicles can recapitulate the selective packaging of the 5' untranslated region of the HIV-1 genome in the presence of excess competitor RNA.
source: We used a minimal system consisting of purified RNAs, recombinant HIV-1 Gag and giant unilamellar vesicles to recapitulate the selective packaging of the 5' untranslated region of the HIV-1 genome in the presence of excess competitor RNA.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the study, supported by data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Mutations in the CA-CTD domain of Gag which subtly affect the self-assembly of Gag abrogated RNA selectivity.
source: Mutations in the CA-CTD domain of Gag which subtly affect the self-assembly of Gag abrogated RNA selectivity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: tRNA suppresses Gag membrane binding less when Gag has bound viral RNA.
source: We further found that tRNA suppresses Gag membrane binding less when Gag has bound viral RNA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The ability of HIV-1 Gag to selectively package its RNA genome and its self-assembly on membranes are interdependent on one another.
source: The ability of HIV-1 Gag to selectively package its RNA genome and its self-assembly on membranes are thus interdependent on one another.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that mutations affecting assembly also affect RNA selectivity.

claim: The nucleocapsid (NC) domain of Gag has two zinc knuckle motifs which together with adjacent residues interact with the viral RNA.
source: The nucleocapsid (NC) domain of Gag has two zinc knuckle motifs which together with adjacent residues interact with the viral RNA (Berkowitz et al., 1993; Lu et al., 2011b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mutations in NC that interfere with RNA binding lead to formation of non-infectious viruses.
source: Mutations in NC that interfere with RNA binding lead to formation of non-infectious viruses (Aldovini and Young, 1990; Gorelick et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Gag selectively packages unspliced, full-length genomic RNA through interactions with its 5' untranslated region (5'UTR).
source: Gag selectively packages unspliced, full-length genomic RNA through interactions with its 5' untranslated region (5'UTR), which is different in spliced and unspliced constructs (Lu et al., 2011b; Kuzembayeva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: >90% of released HIV-1 particles have packaged genomic RNA.
source: Single-virion fluorescence assays indicate that >90% of released HIV-1 particles have packaged genomic RNA (Chen et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Packaging of a dimeric genome appears to be strongly preferred.
source: packaging of a dimeric genome appears to be strongly preferred (Sakuragi et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2009; Nikolaitchik et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The packaging of a single dimeric genome is independent of RNA mass, since genomes with altered lengths are always packaged as single dimers.
source: The packaging of a single dimeric genome is independent of RNA mass, since genomes with altered lengths are always packaged as single dimers (Nikolaitchik et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Genomic RNAs with sequence differences are efficiently packaged as heterodimers as long as they have identical DIS sequences.
source: Genomic RNAs with sequence differences are efficiently packaged as heterodimers as long as they have identical DIS sequences (Chen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The ψ/SL3 stem loop region in the 5'UTR was initially identified as a sequence required for efficient packaging of genomic RNA into HIV-1 virions.
source: The ψ/SL3 stem loop region in the 5'UTR was initially identified as a sequence required for efficient packaging of genomic RNA into HIV-1 virions (Lever et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: A single released HIV-1 virus contains one dimeric genomic RNA and 2400 ± 700 Gag molecules.
source: A single released HIV-1 virus contains one dimeric genomic RNA (Chen et al., 2009) and 2400 ± 700 Gag molecules (Carlson et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cross-linking-immunoprecipitation sequencing (CLIP-seq) revealed a strikingly different RNA preference of cytosolic and membrane-bound Gag.
source: Indeed, cross-linking-immunoprecipitation sequencing (CLIP-seq) revealed a strikingly different RNA preference of cytosolic and membrane-bound Gag (Kutluay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cytosolic Gag binds tRNA through its otherwise membrane-binding matrix (MA) domain.
source: Cytosolic Gag binds tRNA through its otherwise membrane-binding matrix (MA) domain
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Kutluay et al., 2014 in the same paragraph.

claim: Cytosolic Gag associates mainly with cellular RNAs through its NC domain.
source: Cytosolic Gag binds tRNA through its otherwise membrane-binding matrix (MA) domain, and associates mainly with cellular RNAs through its NC domain.
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Kutluay et al., 2014 in the same paragraph.

claim: The minor fraction of cytosolic Gag which binds viral RNA has a strong preference for the 5'UTR but also binds to the Rev-responsive element (RRE).
source: The minor fraction of cytosolic Gag which binds viral RNA has a strong preference for the 5'UTR but also binds to the Rev-responsive element (RRE), whose main function is thought to be in nuclear export (Kuzembayeva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Gag in the membrane fraction has lost its tRNA association and is strongly enriched for viral RNA, interacting with equal probability with all parts of the genomic RNA.
source: On the other hand, Gag in the membrane fraction has lost its tRNA association and is strongly enriched for viral RNA, interacting with equal probability with all parts of the genomic RNA.
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Kutluay et al., 2014 in the same paragraph.

claim: GUV-bound Gag clusters mimic the behavior of cellular HIV-1 budding sites in their lipid requirements for assembly, nucleic acid- and ESCRT protein binding.
source: We showed that GUV-bound Gag clusters mimic the behavior of cellular HIV-1 budding sites in their lipid requirements for assembly, nucleic acid- and ESCRT (endosomal sorting complex required for transport) protein binding.
evidence: This is a reference to the authors' previous work (Carlson and Hurley, 2012).

claim: The 1–345 construct was previously shown to dimerize even in the absence of Gag.
source: The 1–345 construct was previously shown to dimerize even in the absence of Gag (Heng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Strong RNA fluorescence was consistently observed at Gag clusters on GUV membranes, regardless of which RNA was used.
source: Strong RNA fluorescence was consistently observed at Gag clusters on GUV membranes, regardless of which RNA was used (Figure 1a–c,g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: RNA recruitment to Gag clusters was dependent on the NC domain of Gag.
source: This RNA recruitment was dependent on the NC domain of Gag since neither a ΔNC Gag nor Gag treated with the Zn-finger disrupting drug AT-2 (Rossio et al., 1998) was able to recruit fluorescent RNA to GUV membranes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: When a ten fold excess of non-fluorescent RNA378 was included, the fluorescent 5'UTR was still visible at most Gag clusters, whereas RRE was present at fewer Gag clusters and at lower fluorescence intensities, and fluorescent RNA378 was virtually absent.
source: After assembly on GUVs, the fluorescent 5'UTR was still visible at most Gag clusters in the presence of ten fold excess competitor RNA, whereas RRE was present at fewer Gag clusters and at lower fluorescence intensities, and fluorescent RNA378 was virtually absent (Figure 1d–f,g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: 5'UTR 3way1 has several packaging-critical guanines around the three-way junction 1 in the CES mutated to adenines (G116A, G318A, G320A, G328A, G329A, G331A, G333A).
source: 5'UTR 3way1 has several packaging-critical guanines around the three-way junction 1 in the CES mutated to adenines (G116A, G318A, G320A, G328A, G329A, G331A, G333A).
evidence: This describes the mutations introduced in the 5'UTR 3way1 construct.

claim: The set of mutations in 5'UTR 3way1 was previously found to reduce packaging in a cellular packaging assay.
source: This set of mutations was previously found to reduce packaging in a cellular packaging assay (Keane et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: 5'UTR mono has the GCGCGC sequence in DIS replaced by GAGA, creating a monomeric 5'UTR.
source: 5'UTR mono has the GCGCGC sequence in DIS replaced by GAGA, creating a monomeric 5'UTR.
evidence: This describes the mutations introduced in the 5'UTR mono construct.

claim: In the presence of 5 nM 5'UTR very little fluorescent 5'UTR could be seen at Gag clusters on GUVs.
source: In the presence of 5 nM 5'UTR very little fluorescent 5'UTR could be seen at Gag clusters on GUVs (Figure 2b,g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the presence of either of the altered constructs, more fluorescent 5'UTR was visible at Gag clusters.
source: However, in the presence of either of the altered constructs, more fluorescent 5'UTR was visible at Gag clusters (Figure 2c–f,g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The in vitro packaging assay is able to detect the lower affinity of assembling Gag for monomeric, 3way1-mutated, and spliced 5'UTRs.
source: Thus, the in vitro packaging assay is able to detect the lower affinity of assembling Gag for monomeric, 3way1-mutated, and spliced 5'UTRs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: A minimal system consisting of purified RNAs, Gag, and PI(4,5)P2-containing GUVs recapitulates the selective RNA packaging of an assembling HIV-1 particle at RNA concentrations far below reported solution affinities of NC for 5'UTR.
source: In summary, a minimal system consisting of purified RNAs, Gag, and PI(4,5)P2-containing GUVs recapitulates the selective RNA packaging of an assembling HIV-1 particle at RNA concentrations far below reported solution affinities of NC for 5'UTR.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings, supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The 5'UTR is strongly selected for in a competition assay, whereas the RRE is only partially selected for after addition of competitor.
source: The 5'UTR is strongly selected for in a competition assay, whereas the RRE is only partially selected for after addition of competitor.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: 5'UTRs that are either monomerized, have packaging-critical guanines mutated to adenines, or represent a spliced viral RNA are less favored in the competition assay.
source: 5'UTRs that are either monomerized, have packaging-critical guanines mutated to adenines, or represent a spliced viral RNA are less favored in the competition assay.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The reported affinity constant for 5'UTR-NC association is 17 nM.
source: Given the low concentrations at which this selectivity is observed, below the reported 17 nM affinity constant for 5'UTR-NC association (Heng et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The W316D,M317D mutation alters a motif at the two fold symmetry contact in the CA C-terminal domain (CA-CTD), which is described in the literature to be important for virus assembly.
source: The W316D,M317D mutation ("Gag two-fold") alters a motif at the two fold symmetry contact in the CA C-terminal domain (CA-CTD), which is described in the literature to be important for virus assembly (Gamble et al., 1997; von Schwedler et al., 2003) (Figure 3a–b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: When Gag two-fold protein was added to GUVs at 100 nM, it bound in a strikingly different way from wild-type Gag, often resulting in a diffuse Gag fluorescence covering the entire GUV membrane.
source: When this protein was added to GUVs at 100 nM, it bound in a strikingly different way from wild-type Gag, often resulting in a diffuse Gag fluorescence covering the entire GUV membrane (Figure 3f,g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Wild type Gag essentially only bound to GUVs in clusters even in the absence of RNA.
source: For comparison, wild type Gag essentially only bound to GUVs in clusters even in the absence of RNA (Figure 3e,g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Gag three-fold protein bound GUVs similarly to wild-type Gag, albeit with a moderate increase in the diffuse binding first observed for Gag two-fold.
source: This protein bound GUVs similarly to wild-type Gag, albeit with a moderate increase in the diffuse binding first observed for Gag two-fold (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A Gag protein mutated at the six fold interface in CA-CTD with the single-residue replacement K290A showed an increase in diffuse Gag binding over wild-type Gag.
source: A Gag protein mutated at the six fold interface in CA-CTD (Figure 3a,d) with the single-residue replacement K290A ("Gag six-fold") reported to affect virus assembly (von Schwedler et al., 2003; Robinson et al., 2014), also showed an increase in diffuse Gag binding over wild-type Gag (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Combining the two-, three-, and six-fold mutations in one protein resulted in an assembly phenotype similar to that of Gag two-fold.
source: Combining the two-, three-, and six-fold mutations in one protein ("Gag 2-,3-,6-fold") resulted in an assembly phenotype similar to that of Gag two-fold (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mutations in the CA-CTD of either the W316,M317 motif at the two-fold symmetry contact, or of K290 at the six-fold symmetry contact, both described as leading to virus release defects, affect the ability of Gag to cluster on membranes.
source: Taken together, mutations in the CA-CTD of either the W316,M317 motif at the two-fold symmetry contact, or of K290 at the six-fold symmetry contact, both described as leading to virus release defects (von Schwedler et al., 2003), affect the ability of Gag to cluster on membranes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The presence of RNA increased the clustering of all Gag proteins, and increased the fraction of GUVs which had bound Gag.
source: We observed that the presence of RNA increased the clustering of all Gag proteins, and increased the fraction of GUVs which had bound Gag (Figure 4a–j, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Recruitment of fluorescent 5'UTR to the GUV membrane was observed for all Gag constructs.
source: Recruitment of fluorescent 5'UTR to the GUV membrane was observed for all Gag constructs (Figure 4a–e)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Wild type Gag retained as much 5'UTR fluorescence in the presence of competitor RNA as in its absence.
source: Wild type Gag retained as much 5'UTR fluorescence in the presence of competitor RNA as in its absence (Figure 4f,k)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The Gag three-fold mutant showed only a minor decrease in 5'UTR fluorescence in the presence of competitor RNA.
source: and the Gag three-fold mutant showed only a minor decrease (Figure 4h,k).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: GUV-bound clusters of the Gag two-fold, Gag six-fold and Gag two-, three-, six-fold mutants lost most of their 5'UTR fluorescence in the presence of competitor RNA.
source: On the other hand, GUV-bound clusters of the Gag two-fold, Gag six-fold and Gag two-, three-, six-fold mutants lost most of their 5'UTR fluorescence in the presence of competitor RNA (Figure 4g,i–k).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: RNA selectivity in this assay closely correlates with clustered binding of Gag to GUVs in the absence of RNA.
source: Thus, RNA selectivity in this assay closely correlates with clustered binding of Gag to GUVs in the absence of RNA (compare Figures 3g and 4k).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Mutations which cause subtle changes in the ability of Gag to multimerize on a membrane drastically decrease the RNA selectivity of assembled Gag clusters, without greatly affecting their ability to bind RNA non-specifically.
source: In summary, mutations which cause subtle changes in the ability of Gag to multimerize on a membrane drastically decrease the RNA selectivity of assembled Gag clusters, without greatly affecting their ability to bind RNA non-specifically.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings, supported by data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The RNA-only SHAPE profile is highly consistent with the recently reported solution structure of the HIV-1 RNA packaging signal.
source: The RNA-only SHAPE profile is highly consistent with the recently reported solution structure of the HIV-1 RNA packaging signal (Keane et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study and comparison with SHAPE data.

claim: The dimer-promoting DIS loop (G257-C262) had no SHAPE reactivity.
source: The dimer-promoting DIS loop (G257-C262) had no SHAPE reactivity.
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The SHAPE reactivity of the SD region G289-G292 is consistent with the reported 3D structure of the dimeric conformation.
source: However, the SHAPE reactivity of the SD region G289-G292 (highlighted with a gray shaded box in Figure 5a) is consistent with the reported 3D structure of the dimeric conformation (Keane et al., 2015), not with the completely unprotected loop proposed for the monomeric 5'UTR (Lu et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5 and citations to previous studies.

claim: A longer 356 nt 5'UTR able to assume both monomer- and a dimer-favoring conformations had a similar SHAPE reactivity to the 345 nt 5'UTR, indicating that it is present mainly as a dimer under the conditions of the study.
source: A longer 356 nt 5'UTR able to assume both monomer- and a dimer-favoring conformations (Heng et al., 2012) had a similar SHAPE reactivity to the 345 nt 5'UTR (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b), indicating that it is present mainly as a dimer under the conditions of the study.
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The SHAPE profiles for 5'UTR were very similar in the presence of NC, ΔMA-Gag, and when bound to Gag clusters on GUVs.
source: The SHAPE profiles for 5'UTR were very similar in the presence of NC, ΔMA-Gag, and when bound to Gag clusters on GUVs (Figure 5b, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Upon Gag binding, major SHAPE changes were observed in the following clusters: U117-U122, G234-A242, A271-G273, and A302-G309.
source: Upon Gag binding, major SHAPE changes were observed in the following clusters: U117-U122, G234-A242, A271-G273, and A302-G309 (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5.

claim: GUV recruitment of the complex did not trigger additional SHAPE changes, indicating that the overall structure of the 5'UTR is not further altered between the states of initial Gag binding in solution and recruitment to assembled Gag on a membrane.
source: However, GUV recruitment of the complex did not trigger additional SHAPE changes (Figure 5c, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the overall structure of the 5'UTR is not further altered between the states of initial Gag binding in solution and recruitment to assembled Gag on a membrane.
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5 and is an inference from the data.

claim: The SHAPE reactivity of the SD region G289-G292 is similar under all conditions studied, indicating that the 5'UTR is maintained in the dimeric conformation over the assembly process.
source: Noteworthy, the SHAPE reactivity of the SD region G289-G292 is similar under all conditions studied (Figure 5a,c, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the 5'UTR is maintained in the dimeric conformation over the assembly process.
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5 and is an inference from the data.

claim: There is no evidence for large changes in secondary structures in the 5'UTR when interacting with either Gag in solution or assembled Gag on a membrane, and it appears dimeric under the conditions studied.
source: Taken together, we see no evidence for large changes in secondary structures in the 5'UTR when interacting with either Gag in solution or assembled Gag on a membrane, and it appears dimeric under the conditions studied.
evidence: This is a summary of the SHAPE analysis findings, supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: The membrane-binding matrix (MA) domain of cytosolic Gag has been shown to bind primarily tRNA in cells.
source: The membrane-binding matrix (MA) domain of cytosolic Gag has been shown to bind primarily tRNA in cells (Kutluay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Several reports have shown that RNA binding to the basic patch on the MA domain of HIV-1 Gag can compete with its ability to bind acidic phospholipids such as PI(4,5)P2.
source: Several reports have shown that RNA binding to the basic patch on the MA domain of HIV-1 Gag can compete with its ability to bind acidic phospholipids such as PI(4,5)P2 (Alfadhli et al., 2009, 2011; Chukkapalli et al., 2010, 2013; Dick et al., 2013; Dick and Vogt, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Premixing 100 nM Gag-ATTO594 with 1 µM yeast tRNA before addition to GUVs led to a virtually complete block in Gag assembly on GUVs.
source: Premixing 100 nM Gag-ATTO594 with 1 µM yeast tRNA before addition to GUVs led to a virtually complete block in Gag assembly on GUVs (Figure 6a–b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: For the tRNA titration, a 50% inhibition of Gag membrane association was evident at 200 nM tRNA.
source: For the tRNA titration, a 50% inhibition of Gag membrane association was evident at 200 nM tRNA (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: At 20 µM tRNA, the amount of Gag found in the vesicle fraction dropped to ~10% of the value seen in the absence of RNA.
source: At 20 µM tRNA, the amount of Gag found in the vesicle fraction dropped to ~10% of the value seen in the absence of RNA (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: In the absence of tRNA, all long viral or unspecific RNAs slightly increased the amount of Gag associated with vesicles.
source: In the absence of tRNA, all these RNAs slightly increased the amount of Gag associated with vesicles (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: In the presence of 20 µM tRNA, the 5'UTR and the longer HIV1947 RNA (which contains the 5'UTR sequence) enhanced membrane association by Gag more than the other RNAs.
source: In the presence of 20 µM tRNA however, the 5'UTR and the longer HIV1947 RNA (which contains the 5'UTR sequence) enhanced membrane association by Gag more than the other RNAs (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: RNA378 had no effect on Gag membrane association in the presence of 20 µM tRNA.
source: RNA378 had no effect on Gag membrane association in the presence of 20 µM tRNA, whereas the effect of RRE or the longer RNA2266 was slight (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: tRNA at micromolar concentrations potently inhibits membrane association of Gag.
source: In summary, tRNA at micromolar concentrations potently inhibits membrane association of Gag.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings, supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Under conditions where tRNA inhibits Gag membrane association, Gag that encounters viral RNA has a higher probability of overcoming that inhibition and associating with membrane.
source: Under such conditions, Gag that encounters viral RNA has a higher probability of overcoming that inhibition and associating with membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The NC domain of Gag is necessary but not sufficient for the selective packaging of the HIV-1 genomic RNA.
source: In summary, our study leads to a model for HIV-1 genome selection where the NC domain of Gag is necessary but not sufficient for the selective packaging of the HIV-1 genomic RNA (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claim: Lattice contacts conferring Gag ability to multimerize on a membrane are crucial for the selective packaging of viral RNA.
source: Lattice contacts conferring Gag ability to multimerize on a membrane are crucial for the selective packaging of viral RNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claim: The 5'UTR is recruited to membranes by multimerized Gag without any gross changes to its secondary structure.
source: The 5'UTR is recruited to membranes by multimerized Gag without any gross changes to its secondary structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SHAPE analysis data.

claim: The association of Gag with tRNA serves to inhibit genome-less virus assembly.
source: Moreover, the association of Gag with tRNA serves to inhibit genome-less virus assembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claim: Genomic RNA is present at the onset of HIV-1 assembly at the plasma membrane, at which point the number of Gag molecules was reported to be below the detection limit of ~12 molecules.
source: Genomic RNA is present at the onset of HIV-1 assembly at the plasma membrane, at which point the number of Gag molecules was reported to be below the detection limit of ~12 molecules (Jouvenet et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cytosolic Gag does not form large oligomers and mainly associates with cellular RNAs.
source: Cytosolic Gag does not form large oligomers (Robinson et al., 2014; Hendrix et al., 2015) and mainly associates with cellular RNAs (Kutluay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A small fraction of cytosolic Gag is found to be slowly diffusing and consist of oligomers of up to ~5 molecules.
source: A small fraction of cytosolic Gag is found to be slowly diffusing and consist of oligomers of up to ~5 molecules (Hendrix et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The large majority of plasma membrane-proximal genomic HIV-1 RNAs are monomeric in the absence of HIV-1 Gag.
source: It was reported that the large majority of plasma membrane-proximal genomic HIV-1 RNAs are monomeric in the absence of HIV-1 Gag.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2016.

claim: In cells expressing Gag, monomeric genomic RNAs are seen to coalesce to dimers on the membrane, but were not observed to arrive to the membrane as dimers.
source: In cells expressing Gag, monomeric genomic RNAs are seen to coalesce to dimers on the membrane, but were not observed to arrive to the membrane as dimers.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2016.

claim: The packaging signal of the related retrovirus Murine Leukemia Virus (MLV) is partially unfolded in released immature virions.
source: This contrasts with reports that the packaging signal of the related retrovirus Murine Leukemia Virus (MLV) is partially unfolded in released immature virions (Grohman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The strongest decrease in SHAPE reactivity upon Gag interaction was found in the guanosine-rich bulges on the DIS stem, consistent with a recent study using full-length Gag in solution.
source: The strongest decrease in SHAPE reactivity upon Gag interaction was found in the guanosine-rich bulges on the DIS stem (Figure 5c), consistent with a recent study using full-length Gag in solution (Abd El-Wahab et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by SHAPE data shown in Figure 5 and a citation to a previous study.

claim: The increased SHAPE reactivity in central regions of the tandem three-way junction suggests that Gag engagement, while not leading to a drastic rearrangement of the 5'UTR secondary structure, may lead to alterations its 3D structure.
source: The increased SHAPE reactivity in central regions of the tandem three-way junction suggests that Gag engagement, while not leading to a drastic rearrangement of the 5'UTR secondary structure, may lead to alterations its 3D structure.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the SHAPE data.

claim: RNA conformational changes upon binding to membrane-associated Gag are minor in magnitude and thus suggest that conformation rearrangements are likely to be a minor contributor to selective packaging.
source: Overall, our results show that RNA conformational changes upon binding to membrane-associated Gag are minor in magnitude and thus suggest that conformation rearrangements are likely to be a minor contributor to selective packaging.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SHAPE analysis data.

claim: Gag-tRNA interactions may serve to increase Gag fidelity for viral RNA.
source: Our reconstituted system allowed us to disentangle the effect that different RNAs have on Gag membrane association (Figure 6). We show that Gag-tRNA interactions may also serve to increase Gag fidelity for viral RNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A viral RNA with several high-affinity binding sites for Gag can recruit several Gag molecules to the membrane if only one of them dissociates from its membrane-occluding tRNA.
source: We hypothesize that a viral RNA with several high-affinity binding sites for Gag can recruit several Gag molecules to the membrane if only one of them dissociates from its membrane-occluding tRNA.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings.

claim: The amount of viral RNA coprecipitated with cytoplasmic Gag is reduced five fold when its CA-CTD is deleted, whereas the amount of cellular RNA coprecipitated remains the same.
source: In line with our findings, it has been reported that the amount of viral RNA coprecipitated with cytoplasmic Gag is reduced five fold when its CA-CTD is deleted, whereas the amount of cellular RNA coprecipitated remains the same (Kutluay and Bieniasz, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: A ΔCA-CTD Gag was still able to tether genomic RNA to the plasma membrane in cells.
source: On the other hand, in experiments which did not address selectivity, a ΔCA-CTD Gag was still able to tether genomic RNA to the plasma membrane in cells (Jouvenet et al., 2009; Sardo et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A ΔCA-NTD Gag still supports particle release.
source: Mutations at the three-fold symmetry contact in CA-NTD did not alter Gag clustering on membranes (Figure 3g), concurring with observations that a ΔCA-NTD Gag still supports particle release (Borsetti et al., 1998; Accola et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: It is possible that the RNA chaperone activity of Gag may be necessary to expose the 5'UTR and its DIS in the context of a full-length genome.
source: It is possible that the RNA chaperone activity of Gag may be necessary to expose the 5'UTR and its DIS in the context of a full-length genome.
evidence: This is a speculation by the authors.
